proof_nl: Let x be an arbitrary real number. By definition, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Therefore floor(x) is itself an integer and satisfies floor(x) ≤ x. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: Use the defining property of the floor function: floor(x) is an integer not exceeding x. Hence floor(x) ≤ x for all real x.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly proves the universal inequality floor(x) ≤ x by unpacking the definition of floor and concluding from arbitrariness of x. It matches the lemma statement exactly and uses no problematic dependencies.
